newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks hit record on 1st trade day under China.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks hit record on 1st trade day under China.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chip Hang Seng Index jumped to a record high at the start of trade on Thursday, the first trading day under Chinese rule, jumping 166 points, or 1.10 percent, to 15,363.

Enthusiasm surrounding Hong Kong's change in sovereignty also swept red chip stocks sharply higher, with the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index surging 81 points, or 2.35 percent, to 3,550.
The Hang Seng Index later shed its gains, falling 94 points, or 0.62 percent, to 15,102 while the red chip index pared its gains to trade up 37 points, or 1.08 percent, at 3,506.
"The market was artificially pumped up," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales at Nava SC Securities.
"But here comes the realisation that we still have this overhang about what is going to happen to the property market."
Property stocks led the blue chips down after Hong Kong's new government announced plans on Tuesday to increase housing supply.
